title: Climbing Stairs
summary: Count the distinct ways to climb n steps taking one or two at a time.
statement:
You are climbing a staircase with `n` steps. Each move takes you up either one step or two. Return how many distinct sequences of moves reach the top.

### Constraints

- 1 ≤ n ≤ 45

> **Where the recursion comes from**
>
> The last move was either one step or two, so the ways to reach step n are the ways to reach n-1 plus the ways to reach n-2. Written as plain recursion that recomputes the same subproblems exponentially and will time out around n = 40; the fix is to remember each answer as you go, which is the whole idea behind the [Dynamic Programming](/tutorials) tutorial.

visibleTests.explanation: 1+1+1, 1+2, or 2+1. Order matters, so 1+2 and 2+1 are different.
The counts follow the Fibonacci numbers.
